posts.content: I am good. Prioritize total payoff of good players: cooperate with good or uncertain opponents; defect only when an opponent is reliably selfish.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize shared welfare; defect against reliably selfish opponents, who tend to defect.
Cooperate with uncertain or likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect only when an opponent is reliably selfish.
Prioritize welfare among good players: cooperate with uncertain or likely-good opponents, and defect only when there is strong evidence an opponent is selfish.
The four opponents observed choosing C are good; cooperate with P8 absent contrary evidence, and update beliefs from each encounter.
Cooperate with uncertain or likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect only when there is strong evidence an opponent is selfish.
P4 is untested. Cooperate unless there is reliable evidence they are selfish; cooperation maximizes welfare if both of us are good.
P9 is untested; cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare, and update beliefs from the encounter.
P9 defected against my cooperation, so treat them as likely selfish. Cooperate with P6 absent evidence otherwise; prioritize welfare of good players.
Final round vs P9, who defected against my C: choose D to avoid exploitation; report P9 as highly likely selfish.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare; adapt to observed behavior in later rounds.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when an opponent is reliably selfish.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support total welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is reliably selfish.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare; defect only when there is strong evidence the opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with P8: cooperation supports welfare when both players are good, and P8 is more likely good. Treat opponents observed cooperating as good and update remaining beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate to support welfare among good players; all five opponents observed cooperating are likely good. Continue cooperating with uncertain opponents and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested P4: they are more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation yields greater total welfare among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with uncertain P9: this supports higher welfare if they are good and ties expected welfare against a selfish opponent. All previous cooperators are inferred good.
Cooperate with P6: if they are good, mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare; if selfish, defecting gains only one point for me while excluding their payoff.
Cooperate in the final round: P9’s defection raises suspicion, but mutual welfare with a good opponent outweighs the limited gain from defecting unless selfishness is highly certain.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player writes a private strategy note that only that player sees. Players cannot send messages to one another.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Gameplay has ended. Report your final private identity beliefs and summarize your
strategy in at most 300 characters. Return beliefs and strategy. This report has
no effect on payoffs and is not a public message.
